biography: Steve Roberts, a name once whispered with promise on the British racing circuit, hails from the sleepy village of Oakington, Cambridgeshire. His passion ignited at the age of 8, watching Nigel Mansell clinch the 1992 World Championship. Roberts pestered his parents relentlessly until they relented, buying him a kart. He quickly rose through the karting ranks, displaying raw talent and an aggressive overtaking style. A defining moment came in the 2012 Formula Renault UK season; leading the championship going into the final race, a clumsy collision while battling for the lead cost him the title. He secured a seat with Firenze Autosports in Formula A six years ago, initially showing flashes of brilliance. However, inconsistent performances and a string of unfortunate mechanical failures have hampered his progress. Now at 34, and with a noticeable decline in performance over the last two seasons, whispers suggest his time in Formula A may be drawing to a close. The fire still burns, but the results aren't there.
drivingStyle: Roberts is known for his aggressive, almost reckless driving style. He attacks corners with gusto, often pushing the car beyond its limits in qualifying. While this approach can yield spectacular results, it often leads to tire degradation and inconsistent race pace. He struggles to manage pressure, often cracking under the weight of expectation when in a leading position. His tire management is subpar, often requiring early pitstops.

rivalries.reason: A bitter rivalry stemming from a controversial incident at Monza in 2020, where Bellini allegedly forced Roberts off the track while battling for the lead.
A constant battle for grid position and points, with both drivers known for their uncompromising racing styles, leading to several on-track clashes.
A clash of egos more than anything. Both drivers believe they are destined for greatness, leading to a tense and competitive atmosphere whenever they are near each other.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of socks gifted to him by his grandmother.
Listens to classical music for precisely 30 minutes before every race to calm his nerves.
Refuses to eat anything green on race day, believing it brings bad luck.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about playing it safe; it's about pushing the boundaries and taking risks. If you're not on the edge, you're not trying hard enough."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2019 Monaco Grand Prix after a daring late-race overtake, securing his first and only Formula A victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the 2021 British Grand Prix at Silverstone, gifting the victory to his rival, Marco Bellini.
